newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DODGERS BEAT BRAVES WITH FOUR-HITTER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DODGERS BEAT BRAVES WITH FOUR-HITTER.

text.p: Pedro Astacio combined with Scott Radinsky on a four-hitter and chipped in with an RBI single as the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 4-1 on Saturday.
Astacio (6-7) won his third straight decision, giving up three hits, including a solo homer to pinch-hitter Tony Graffanino, over 7-1/3 innings.
"Yeah, I know it's over. I don't think about it, I go out there and pitch my game," Astacio said of his 1-9 record against the Braves.
Radinsky allowed one hit and struck out three in 1-1/3 innings. Kevin Millwood (1-1) took the loss in his first major-league start. He surrendered four runs and seven hits in five innings.
In Chicago, the Cubs won a double header against the Colorado Rockies, cruising to a 7-0 victory in the first game and squeaking to a 6-5 win in the nightcap.
Steve Trachsel and Turk Wendell combined on a four-hitter, and Sammy Sosa scored twice and drove in two runs in the first game, the first time the Cubs beat the Rockies in five games this season.
The opener was Chicago's first over the Rockies in five games this season.
Mark Grace's second sacrifice fly of the game snapped an eighth-inning tie to give the Cubs the edge.
Chicago rallied from a 4-0 deficit against former Cub Frank Castillo. The Rockies have lost a season-high eight straight games and are 1-15 in July.

"I'm surprised by our struggles," Colorado manager Don Baylor conceded. "We've got a veteran ballclub. One thing I didn't want to hear this year was about our road woes from '96, but now they are back. We left 14 men on base in the second game and that just puts a stake in your heart."

At Florida, rookie Livan Hernandez allowed just one hit in six shutout innings and Charles Johnson homered twice and drove in three runs to power the Florida Marlins to an 8-5 victory over the San Diego Padres.
Hernandez (3-0), recalled from the minors after the Marlins traded Pat Rapp on Friday, struck out four, walked three and helped himself at the plate with two hits.
San Diego starter Danny Jackson (2-8) was chased after 3 2/3 innings, losing for the eighth time in nine decisions. He surrendered eight hits and six runs.

In Montreal, Jeff Bagwell had three hits, including a two-run homer and scored three runs, and Shane Reynolds overcame a rough start for his first win in 2-1/2 months as the Houston Astros rallied and held on for an 8-6 victory over the slumping Montreal Expos.

Bagwell homered off starter Jeff Juden in the fifth inning to give the Astros a 4-3 lead. He also doubled and scored in the third inning and singled and scored in the ninth. His 26 homers and 88 RBI both are second in the National League.
Derek Bell drove in two runs and Tim Bogar also homered for the Astros, who have won five of their last six games.

In New York, Bernard Gilkey hit a three-run homer in the eighth inning to snap a tie and Rick Reed pitched eight strong innings and helped himself with a two-run homer as the New York Mets defeated the Cincinnati Reds, 5-3.

"He was feeling good about the way he's seeing the ball and has been for a while," said Mets manager Bobby Valentine. "He even said that if he got up he was going to end it. He's got a look in his eye and he's showing a lot of confidence."
Reed (7-4) allowed two runs and six hits to earn his third straight win. After allowing a two-out single to Eric Owens in the fourth inning, Reed retired the last 13 batters he faced.

In Philadelphia, Dale Sveum and Kevin Young drove in three runs apiece and each of the top seven players in the batting order got two hits as the Pittsburgh Pirates hammered the Philadelphia Phillies, 13-3.
All of Pittsburgh's starters, with the exception of pitcher Steve Cooke (8-9), had at least one hit and scored at least once as the Pirates pounded out 17 hits.

In St Louis, Ron Gant blasted a three-run homer in the bottom of the eighth inning as the St. Louis Cardinals rallied to beat the San Francisco Giants for the sixth time in seven tries this season, 8-7.

Doug Henry (2-4) opened the eighth and Royce Clayton reached on an error by shortstop Jose Vizcaino. Delino DeShields walked before Gant belted a 2-1 pitch 402 feet over the left-centre field fence, erasing a 6-5 deficit.
